# Effects

The effects of the rule system itself (05 §10.2 to §10.6). An effect is an object with one key that names it; every other key of a list of effects is a [verb](verbs.md), or a rule with parameters that a mod defines.

<a id="add"></a>
## `add`

`{ "add": { "self.var.kills": 1 } }`

Adds to a number, or appends one element to a list. Something never set counts as nothing: adding a number to it gives that number.

<a id="after"></a>
## `after`

`{ "after": "2 s", "do": […] }`

Runs effects once, later, on the owner's clock (05 §10.4), with the subjects and locals as they are now. `name` (a text unique to the owner; a timer of that name is replaced), `owner` (a subject with a clock; default the rule's `self`, else the realm of `here`, else the simulation) and `while_unloaded` (`pause`, the default, or `elapse`).

<a id="as"></a>
## `as`

`{ "as": { "self": expr }, "do": […] }`

Binds subjects by name for the effects in `do`. Each expression is worked out before any name is bound.

<a id="ask"></a>
## `ask`

`{ "ask": { "who": entity, "prompt": template, "options": [ { "label": template, "if": cond, "do": […] } ] } }`

Offers a choice. A directly controlled entity is asked and time stops until it answers; anyone else takes the first option whose `if` holds. The chosen option's `do` runs with the subjects and locals of where the `ask` is written. `options` may instead be an expression giving a list of maps, each with `label`, `eoc` and `with`. `who` defaults to `self`.

<a id="attach-rule"></a>
## `attach_rule`

`{ "attach_rule": { "to": subject, "eoc": id } }`

Attaches an attached rule to a subject. Attaching one that is already there does nothing.

<a id="cancel-event"></a>
## `cancel_event`

`{ "cancel_event": { "reason": id, "values": { … } } }`

In a rule that handles a hook: prevents what the hook precedes. `reason` is a `reason` definition and `values` what it carries, by name; both may be left out.

<a id="cancel-timer"></a>
## `cancel_timer`

`{ "cancel_timer": "name" }`

Cancels the timer of that name (05 §10.4) of the owner `after` would choose, or of `{ "cancel_timer": { "name": …, "owner": subject } }`. Cancelling none does nothing.

<a id="consume"></a>
## `consume`

`{ "consume": {} }`

Marks the event being handled as consumed: later handlers marked `skip_if_consumed` are skipped.

<a id="detach-rule"></a>
## `detach_rule`

`{ "detach_rule": { "to": subject, "eoc": id } }`

Takes a rule attached at run time off a subject, and forgets when it last ran there.

<a id="emit"></a>
## `emit`

`{ "emit": { "event": id, … } }`

Raises an event a mod defined. The other keys are the event's subjects and fields by name; every subject must be given, and a field left out is null.

<a id="every"></a>
## `every`

`{ "every": "1 s", "times": 5, "do": […] }`

Runs effects after each interval of the owner's clock (05 §10.4), `times` times (an int) or for ever. Takes `name`, `owner` and `while_unloaded` as `after` does, and `all` among the modes: fire once for each interval missed.

<a id="first"></a>
## `first`

`{ "first": [ { "if": cond, "do": […] }, { "do": […] } ] }`

Runs the first entry whose condition holds. An entry with no `if` always holds.

<a id="for-each"></a>
## `for_each`

`{ "for_each": list, "as": "x", "do": […] }`

Runs `do` once for each element of a list, bound to the local `$x`. The list is an expression, `{ "list": expr }`, or a query (05 §11).

<a id="if"></a>
## `if`

`{ "if": cond, "then": […], "else": […] }`

Runs `then` if the condition holds and `else` if it does not. Either list may be left out, not both.

<a id="let"></a>
## `let`

`{ "let": { "x": expr, "y": { "run": … } } }`

Defines locals, in the order written, for the rest of the list they are in. A value is an expression, a value source, `{ "run": … }` for what a rule returns, or `{ "emit": … }` for what came of an event.

<a id="message"></a>
## `message`

`{ "message": { "text": template, "to": entity, "style": string } }`

Puts a line in the message log of whoever controls `to`, written for `to` as its reader (05 §4.6). `to` defaults to `self`; `style` names how the interface shows it. `{ "message": "…" }` gives the text alone.

<a id="modify"></a>
## `modify`

`{ "modify": { "event.energy": expr } }`

In a rule that handles a hook: changes fields the hook declares mutable.

<a id="queue"></a>
## `queue`

`{ "queue": { "eoc": id, "with": { … } } }`

Calls a rule once the rule that is running, and whatever called it, has finished. Its arguments and the subjects it is given are worked out now. Queued rules run in the order they were queued.

<a id="repeat"></a>
## `repeat`

`{ "repeat": n, "do": […] }`

Runs `do` `n` times, an int; the local `$i` counts from zero.

<a id="return"></a>
## `return`

`{ "return": expr }`

Ends this rule and gives a value of the rule's `returns` to whoever called it. Only in a rule.

<a id="run"></a>
## `run`

`{ "run": { "eoc": id, "with": { … } } }`

Calls a rule. `eoc` is the rule's id, or `{ "expr": … }` for one worked out when the effect runs; `with` gives its parameters by name. `{ "run": "id" }` calls a rule that needs none.

<a id="set"></a>
## `set`

`{ "set": { "self.var.kills": expr, "$x": expr } }`

Assigns to places: locals, variables, settable properties, mutable fields of a hook, and entries of those.

<a id="set-rule-group"></a>
## `set_rule_group`

`{ "set_rule_group": { "group": id, "on": bool } }`

Switches a rule group on or off, whatever its `enabled` says. `"on": null` leaves it to `enabled` again.

<a id="stop"></a>
## `stop`

`{ "stop": {} }`

Ends this rule, or this list of effects.

<a id="strike"></a>
## `strike`

`{ "strike": { "attack": id, "target": entity, "part": part, "effort": real, "sure": bool } }`

Only an action's lists may hold it.

Resolves an attack of the action whose list it is written in against `target`, or against the cell `at` (07 §3.4), and leaves `$landed`, `$absorbed` and `$passed` in the action's locals. `attack` may be left out of an action with one attack; `effort` defaults to 1, `sure` to false. Only in an action's lists.

<a id="switch"></a>
## `switch`

`{ "switch": expr, "cases": { "a": […], "b": […] }, "default": […] }`

Runs the case whose key the value reads as: a text as it is, a number as it is written, an id as its qualified id. `default`, which may be left out, runs when no case matches.

<a id="unset"></a>
## `unset`

`{ "unset": [ "self.var.marked" ] }`

Removes variables, so that each reads as its default again, and entries of maps and lists. A local is made null.

<a id="weighted"></a>
## `weighted`

`{ "weighted": [ { "weight": 3, "do": […] }, … ] }`

Runs one entry, chosen at random with the chance its `weight`, a number, gives it. Weights of zero or less are never chosen.

<a id="while"></a>
## `while`

`{ "while": cond, "do": […] }`

Runs `do` for as long as the condition holds, within the step budget.
